The present appeal is filed by appellants M/s Future Consumer Ltd. and Sh.Deepak Gautam against the order dated 09.09.2024 passed by adjudicating authority imposing penalty of Rs.20,000/- each on both the appellants.
2. The matter relates to the product "Panchamrit Tea' and sample thereof was purchased by Sh.

New Delhi- 110024 on 24.06.2019.

One part of the sample was sent to the Food Analyst,
Government of Delhi on 25.06.2019 and remaining parts were separately sealed and were deposited with the designated officer as per rules and regulations.

3. The Food Analyst vide report bearing no. FSS/890/2019 dated 05.07.2019 opined as under:-
"The sample is misbranded because there is violation of Section 23 (1), Section 3 (1)(d), Section 24 (2)(a) of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 and Regulation No.2.3.2 of The Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) & Labelling) Regulation,
2011.".

sentences.text:
'Labelling claim "Cardamom - improves digestion, cloves - Good antioxidant, boosts immunity,
Mace - Reduces stress, cures cold and cough, Basil leaves - page no. 2 of 13 improves digestion and respiration, Nutmeg - Helps in digestion, improves skin,
Saffron - works as antidepressant" are medicinal and therapeutic claims which are not permitted as per Section 23 (1) of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006.

Further the sample gives false declaration regarding composition of food in contravention of Section 3 (1)(d) and 24 (2)(a) of the Food Safety & Standards Act 2006' because it does not declare TEA as one of the ingredient and does not contain other declared ingredients like cloves, basil leaves, saffron, cardamom, mace and nutmeg.

The net weight, code number, date of packaging and best before declaration are not given on the principal display panel of the packet, which is in violation of Regulation No.2.3.2 of the Food Safety & Standards (Packaging & Labelling) Regulation, 2011."

4. The requisite application was filed before Adjudicating Officer, ADM, South-East and after following due process (opportunity to file an appeal was not availed by the respondent under Section 46 (4) of Food Safety Standards Act 2006) penalty was imposed upon companies and authorised officers involved in manufacturing, supply and distribution.
page no. 3 of 13 5.
The impugned order has been assailed on the grounds that the order of Adjudicating Officer is bad in law, erroneous and not tenable and therefore, liable to be set aside.

Adjudicating Officer failed to appreciate that during the course of business the appellants herein has taken all the measures in accordance with Food Safety and Standard Act 2006, Rules and Regulations made there under and any other applicable laws.
Food article / sample in question was purchased from M/s Marvel Ltd, Marvel Road, UK lana, Haryana.
It is admitted case of the complainant FSO that the sampled commodity were in sealed condition as packed and received from the manufacturer.

Appellant is protected by guarantee as enumerated under Section 26 (4) of the Food Safety and Standards Act which provides that "a bill, cash memo or invoice in respect of sale of any article of food given by a food business operator to the vendor shall be deemed to be a guarantee under this section, even if a guarantee in the specified form is not included in the bill, cash memo or invoice M/S Future Consumer Ltd vs State (Fso) on 20 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175281257/
2 and thus are entitled to get the benefit of guarantee by manufacturer and thus liable to be discharged from present adjudicating proceedings.
6.

It is further stated that appellants are protected by the defence of Due Diligence as incorporated in Section 80 (b) (2) (d) (I) by the FSS Act 2006 and the guarantee as provided in Section 26 (4) and 27 of FSS Act 2006.
Appellant do not exercise any control over the product / sample in question in its process of manufacturing and labelling and packaging of the page no. 4 of 13 same.
Appellants must be considered as bonafide consumer of this product.

Food Analyst Laboratory, Delhi was not competent to Analyse the sample commodity as per Section 43 of the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006, as it was neither NABL Accredited nor notified in the Gazette by the FSSAI.
It is prayed that impugned order be set aside.
7. Arguing on behalf of appellants, Ld. Counsel has submitted that sample of Tea taken in sealed condition was supplied to the appellants from the manufacturer M/s Marvel Ltd.
Appellants had no role in the manufacturing, packing, or labelling of the sample commodity and appellants dealt only with goods received in sealed condition from the manufacturer.
They exercised due diligence by purchasing against valid invoices and were selling in the same form.
Liability, if any, rests solely with the manufacturer and mere possession of sealed goods cannot attract penalty.
Appellants are entitled to guarantee under Section 26 (4) along with Section 80 (2)(d)(i) of the FSS Act 2006.
The penalty cannot be sustained in law as the Food Analyst's report itself is defective.

sentences.text: The report of Food Analyst dated 05.07.2019 is relied upon which specifically mentions that the claims made on the label were relating to medicinal and therapeutic claims and are not permitted as per Section 23 (1) of Food Safety & Standards Act 2006 as also it was containing false declaration regarding composition of food specially the Tea is not declared as one of the ingredients.
The net weight, code number, date of packing and best before declaration are not given on the principal display panel of the packet.
Therefore, this is a clear case of violations of regulations relating to Food Safety Standards.

I have given due consideration to the contentions of both the sides.

11. The definition of 'Food Business Operator' as per The food Safety and Standards Act 2006 is as follows:-
"Food business operator" in relation to food business means a person by whom the business is carried on or owned and is responsible for ensuring the compliance of this Act, rules and regulations made thereunder".

The definition of 'Misbranding' as per The food Safety and Standards Act 2006 is as follows:-
(zf) misbranded food means an article of food- (A) if it is purported, or is represented to be, or is being- (i) offered or promoted for sale with false, misleading or deceptive claims either;
(a) upon the label of the package, or (b) through advertisement, or (ii) sold by a name which belongs to another article of food; or (iii) offered or promoted for sale under the name of a fictitious individual or company as the manufacturer or producer of the article as borne on the package or containing the article or the label on such package; or page no. 7 of 13 (B) if the article is sold in packages which have been sealed or prepared by or at the instance of the manufacturer or producer bearing his name and address but- (i) the article is an imitation of, or is a substitute for, or resembles in a manner likely to deceive, another article of food under the name of which it is sold, and is not plainly and conspicuously labelled so as to indicate its true character; or M/S Future Consumer Ltd vs State (Fso) on 20 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175281257/
4

(ii) the package containing the article or the label on the package bears any statement, design or device regarding the ingredients or the substances contained therein, which is false or misleading in any material particular, or if the package is otherwise deceptive with respect to its contents; or (iii) the article is offered for sale as the product of any place or country which is false;
or (C) if the article contained in the package- (i) contains any artificial flavouring, colouring or chemical preservative and the package is without a declaratory label stating that fact or is not labelled in accordance with the requirements of this Act or regulations made thereunder or is in contravention thereof; or (ii) is offered for sale for special dietary uses, unless its label bears such information as may be specified by regulation, concerning its vitamins, minerals or other dietary properties in order sufficiently to inform its purchaser as to its value for such use; or page no. 8 of 13 Section 26 of The food Safety and Standards Act 2006:-
Responsibilities of the Food business operator.-(1) Every food business operator shall ensure that the articles of food satisfy the requirements of this Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder at all stages of production, processing, import,
distribution and sale within the businesses under his control.

(2) No food business operator shall himself or by any person on his behalf manufacture, store, sell or distribute any article of food- (i) which is unsafe; or (ii)
which is misbranded or sub-standard or contains extraneous matter; or (iii) for which a licence is required, except in accordance with the conditions of the licence; or (iv) which is for the time being prohibited by the Food Authority or the Central Government or the State Government in the interest of public health; or (v) in contravention of any other provision of this Act or of any rule or regulation made thereunder.
(3) No food business operator shall employ any person who is suffering from infectious, contagious or loathsome disease.

(4) No food business operator shall sell or offer for sale any article of food to any vendor unless he also gives a guarantee in writing in the form specified by regulations about the nature and quality of such article to the vendor: Provided that a bill, cash memo, or invoice in respect of the sale of any article of food given by a food business operator to the vendor shall be deemed to page no. 9 of 13 be a guarantee under this section, even if a guarantee in the specified form is not included in the bill, cash memo or invoice.

(5) Where any food which is unsafe is part of a batch, lot or consignment of food of the same class or description, it shall be presumed that all the food in that batch, lot or consignment is also unsafe, unless following a detailed assessment within a specified time, it is found that there is no evidence that the rest of the batch, lot or consignment is unsafe:
Provided that any conformity of a food with specific provisions applicable to that food shall be without prejudice to the competent authorities taking appropriate measures M/S Future Consumer Ltd vs State (Fso) on 20 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175281257/
5 to impose restrictions on that food being placed on the market or to require its withdrawal from the market for the reasons to be recorded in writing where such authorities suspect that, despite the conformity, the food is unsafe.
Section 27 of The food Safety and Standards Act 2006:-
27. Liability of manufacturers, packers, wholesalers, distributors and sellers.-(1)
The manufacturer or packer of an article of food shall be liable for such article of food if it does not meet the requirements of this Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder.

(2) The wholesaler or distributor shall be liable under this Act for any article of food which is- (a) supplied after the date of its expiry; or (b) stored or supplied in violation of the safety instructions of the manufacturer; or (c) unsafe or misbranded; or (d) unidentifiable of page no. 10 of 13 manufacturer from whom the article of food have been received; or (e) stored or handled or kept in violation of the provisions of this Act, the rules and regulations made thereunder; or (f) received by him with knowledge of being unsafe.

(3) The seller shall be liable under this Act for any article of food which is- (a) sold after the date of its expiry; or (b) handled or kept in unhygienic conditions; or (c) misbranded; or (d) unidentifiable of the manufacturer or the distributors from whom such articles of food were received; or (e) received by him with knowledge of being unsafe.

Section 80 of The food Safety and Standards Act 2006:-
80. Defences which may or may not be allowed in prosecution under this Act.-(A)
Defence relating to publication of advertisements- (B) Defence of due diligence-- (1) In any proceedings for an offence, it is a defence if it is proved that the person took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of the offence by such person or by another person under the person's control.

(2) Without limiting the ways in which a person may satisfy the requirements of clause (1), a person satisfies those requirements if it is proved-- (a) that the commission of the offence was due to-- (i)
an act or default of another person; or (ii) reliance on information page no. 11 of 13 supplied by another person; and (b) (i) the person carried out all such checks of the food concerned as were reasonable in all the circumstances; or (ii) it was reasonable in all the circumstances to rely on checks carried out by the person who supplied such food to the person; and (c) that the person did not import the food into the jurisdiction from another country; and (d) in the case of an offence involving the sale of food, that-- (i) the person sold the food in the same condition as and when the person purchased it; or (ii) the person sold the food in a different condition to that in which the person purchased it, but that the M/S Future Consumer Ltd vs State (Fso) on 20 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175281257/
6 difference did not result in any contravention of this Act or the rules and regulations made thereunder; and 12. On perusal of form VA dated 24.06.2019 (Form of Notice to the Food Business Operator) given by Food Safety Officer, it is clear that contents have been mentioned on the display panel and the Tea is clearly indicated.
Also there are certain medicinal and therapeutic claims made on the display panel but the same are false declarations.

The appellants were supplying the product in the original condition as received from the manufacturing company and although they have no role to play in the preparation of the product, its labelling and packaging but their responsibility under the Act and rules and regulations is very much there. The appellants cannot escape the liability under the law relating to food safety standards.

It is important to note that other respondents who were involved in manufacturing, page no. 12 of 13 selling and distribution and who have been penalised, have not come forward to challenge the findings of adjudicating authority.

13. The provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act provide for liability and responsibility for distributors and appellants having been involved in the supply chain are also responsible as falling in the category of food business operator.

14. On giving due consideration to the facts and circumstances of the present case and relevant legal position, I find no illegality and impropriety in the impugned order dated 09.09.2024 of adjudicating authority.
No interference is called for.
Appeal is accordingly dismissed.
15. Copy of this order and record of FSO be sent to the concerned authority.
16. Appeal file be consigned to the record room.
